## Lock and cap

A machine-local per-branch lock under `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/` prevents
concurrent fixers and reviews of the same feature tree. The ownership-stamped
layout is shared with review and merge: PID, random UUID token, directory
identity, and a digest of complete structured owner metadata. A newer fixer
receives the current complete claim from the serialized acquisition attempt,
then revalidates that exact identity and owner digest under the persistent
sibling mutex before writing a claim-bound cancellation record. If the
directory or owner changed in between, the replacement is not cancelled. Loss
of ownership or a malformed owner/cancellation record stops the holder at a
boundary.
Cancellation before local advancement stops it cleanly; cancellation after a
wrapper-owned commit starts no new phase. Any phase already running completes
at most its one wrapper commit, after which only ownership/comparison checks and
the original-head leased push remain, so no committed tip is stranded. Shell
command failures remain nonzero even inside phase-status handling; interrupt
and termination signals release only the owned lease and retain their signal
exit status. Cap-time release and signal cleanup use the same exact claim and
never remove another process's lease. Ownerless, malformed, or partial locks
remain for explicit operator recovery. No lock file is committed.

The combined iteration count is derived from the complete GitHub-visible PR
commit history. Only subjects beginning exactly with the two fix prefixes
count. GitHub's PR-commits endpoint exposes at most 250 commits, so a history
that cannot be proven complete is a hard failure. At the configured cap, the

   258	def atomic_write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:

   230	# resolve_worktree <branch> — same resolution order as ci.sh: git's own
   231	# worktree registry first, then the .worktrees/<branch> convention. Creates it if the
   232	# branch has no worktree yet.
   233	resolve_worktree() {
   234	  local branch="$1" found="" safe dest have
   235	  found="$(git -C "$ROOT" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null |
   236	    awk -v b="refs/heads/$branch" '
   237	      /^worktree /{p=substr($0,10)}
   238	      $0 == "branch " b {print p; exit}')"
   239	  if [ -n "$found" ] && [ -d "$found" ]; then
   240	    printf '%s\n' "$found"
   241	    return 0
   242	  fi
   243	  safe="$(printf '%s' "$branch" | tr '/' '-')"
   244	  dest="$ROOT/.worktrees/$safe"
   245	  if [ -e "$dest" ]; then
   246	    have="$(git -C "$dest" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
   247	    if [ "$have" = "$branch" ]; then
   248	      printf '%s\n' "$dest"
   249	      return 0
   250	    fi
   251	    die "$dest exists but is not a worktree of '$branch' (HEAD: ${have:-not a git worktree}); run 'git -C $ROOT worktree prune' or remove it"
   252	  fi
   253	  mkdir -p "$ROOT/.worktrees"
   254	  git -C "$ROOT" worktree add --quiet "$dest" "$branch" ||
   255	    die "git worktree add $dest $branch failed"
   256	  if [ -x "$ROOT/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" ]; then
   257	    "$ROOT/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" "$dest" >&2 ||
   258	      warn "worktree-setup.sh failed for $dest; the reviewer runs without a warmed build cache"
   259	  else
   260	    warn "local/bin/worktree-setup.sh not found; the reviewer worktree has no warmed Lean build cache (local/protocols/build-cache.md)"
   261	  fi
   262	  printf '%s\n' "$dest"
   263	}

   265	# run_agent <role> <sandbox> <worktree> <persona-path> <task-file>
   266	#           <standalone-prompt> <context-file> <out-file> <model>
   267	#
   268	# All codex invocations go through local/bin/dispatch.sh when it exists, so the
   269	# session lands in results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl (DESIGN.md, "Agent
   270	# sessions"). There is no direct-execution fallback.
   271	run_agent() {

   274	  local dlog="$out.dispatch.log" task_text last rc=0

   302	    fi

   304	      warn "dispatch.sh exited $rc; its output is at $dlog"
   305	    fi
   306	    return "$rc"
   307	  fi
   308	  die "local/bin/dispatch.sh is required; direct codex execution would lose session telemetry"

item.text: The helper itself does preserve replacement directories for cooperative participants and fails closed on incomplete records. The next risk surface is caller behavior around boundaries: ignored release failures are intentionally fail-safe, but publication and cancellation paths still need to prove that the exact lease and exact PR comparison remain current at the write itself.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	#
     3	# autofix.sh — serialized, capped auto-fix loop for a GitHub PR.
     4	#
     5	# Usage:
     6	#   local/bin/autofix.sh <github-pr-number> --mode {ci|blueprint|review|auto} [--dry-run]
     7	#
     8	#   <github-pr-number> Positive GitHub pull-request number.
     9	#   --mode ci         fix Lean build errors, if the CI manifest says build failed
    10	#          blueprint  fix blueprint compilation, if that CI step failed
    11	#          review     fix unresolved review findings (needs the auto-fix label)
    12	#          auto       dispatch from the CI manifest and run every applicable fix
    13	#                     strictly in the order ci -> blueprint -> review
    14	#   --dry-run   Resolve the dispatch and build the prompts, then stop.
    15	#
    16	# Local replacement for .github/workflows/auto-fix.yml (setup + auto-fix-ci +
    17	# auto-fix-blueprint + auto-fix-review).  Protocol: local/protocols/autofix.md.
    18	#
    19	# Exit codes:
    20	#   0  fixes applied, or an intentional skip (kill switch, nothing to fix,
    21	#      superseded by a newer run, iteration cap reached)
    22	#   1  usage or environment error
    23	#   2  a fix phase failed (agent error, or a rejected commit)
    24	#
    25	# Environment:
    26	#   LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED    disables every fix path on the literal string
    27	#                             "false" only; unset means enabled.
    28	#   MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP         combined fix-iteration cap (default 5)
    29	#   MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF     git ref the fixer personas are read from
    30	#                             (default: main).  Never the branch being fixed.
    31	#   MIPSTARRE_FIX_MODEL       codex model (default: the dispatcher's default)
    32	#   MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT       runtime state root (default ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev)
    33	#   MIPSTARRE_FIX_LOCK_WAIT   seconds to wait for a superseded fix to stop
    34	#                             (default 900)
    35	#   MIPSTARRE_LOG_TAIL_LINES  log lines handed to the fixer (default 400)
    36	#
    37	set -euo pipefail
    38	
    39	PROG="autofix.sh"

   115	src, dest, max_lines = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
   116	try:
   117	    raw = open(src, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
   118	except OSError:

   120	raw = raw.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")

   122	for ch in raw:
   123	    o = ord(ch)

   125	        keep.append(ch)

   129	    truncated = len(lines) - max_lines

   131	out = []
   132	if truncated:
   133	    out.append("... [%d earlier lines dropped by autofix.sh; full log on disk]"

   135	for line in lines:
   136	    line = line.replace("```", "'''").replace("~~~", "'''")
   137	    if line.startswith("<<<") or line.startswith("# Task"):
   138	        line = " " + line

   144	# acquire_fix_lock <lockdir> <wait-seconds> <label>

   147	# auto-fix.yml:259-261).  Reviews use a per-PR lock without cancellation; the
   148	# split is deliberate (auto-fix.yml:29-32).
   149	acquire_fix_lock() {

   151	  local result rc=0 state identity observed_token digest detail

   166	      LOCK_PID="$holder"

   178	(pid ${holder:-unknown}); requesting supersession"

   422	# First-run seeding: when the hot checkout has no .lake/build but the PRIMARY
   423	# checkout holds one under the same keyhash, clone it copy-on-write instead of
   424	# recompiling ~9000 modules from source.  This is the local analogue of the
   425	# parent CI's restore-by-key-prefix (pr-ci.yml:144-160): an older-than-target
   426	# build is fine, Lake rebuilds the delta by trace hash; a keyhash mismatch

   428	# path is correct.  Only .lake is copied — the hot checkout's git state stays
   429	# authoritative.

   431	  local primary="$1"
   432	  [ -d "$HOT_REPO/.lake/build" ] && return 0

   435	    warn "primary checkout keyhash differs from the hot checkout; not seeding .lake from it"
   436	    return 0

   441	    warn "seeding .lake/build from $primary failed; building from source instead"

   453	# rename(2) over an existing symlink.  `mv` is NOT usable here: BSD mv stat()s the
   454	# destination, follows the old `current` symlink to its directory, and would move
   455	# the new link *inside* the snapshot instead of replacing it.
   456	atomic_symlink() { # <target> <linkpath>
   457	  python3 - "$1" "$2" <<'PY'
   458	import os
   459	import sys
   460	
   461	target, link = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   462	tmp = "%s.tmp.%d" % (link, os.getpid())
   463	if os.path.islink(tmp) or os.path.exists(tmp):
   464	    os.remove(tmp)
   465	os.symlink(target, tmp)
   466	os.replace(tmp, link)
   467	PY

   508	# The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround (docgen.yml:56-69).  `lake exe cache get`
   509	# runs `lake update`, whose mathlib post-update hook prunes
   510	# .lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib before fetching a cloud release; on a
   511	# tree that has never built, the directory does not exist and the uncaught
   512	# exception aborts the whole cache fetch.  Locally the same fetch also aborts when
   513	# a vendored package tree is *dirty* — build byproducts such as
   514	# widget/js/lake.trace block the revision checkout; see the 2026-08-30 failure and
   515	# its retry in results/telemetry/builds.jsonl.  Both are fresh-state bugs, and a
   516	# pristine checkout is exactly fresh state.
   517	proofwidgets_fresh_state_workaround() { # <tree>
   518	  local tree="$1" pkg name
   519	  [ -d "$tree/.lake/packages" ] || return 0
   520	  # Only tracked modifications are reset.  `git clean` is deliberately NOT run
   521	  # inside a vendored package: it would delete downloaded build output and cost
   522	  # hours to refetch.  If an untracked byproduct still blocks the checkout, the
   523	  # cache fetch fails loudly and the caller falls back to compiling from source.
   524	  for pkg in "$tree"/.lake/packages/*; do

   530	        || warn "could not reset $name; the Mathlib cache fetch may abort"
   531	    fi

   534	    mkdir -p "$tree/.lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib"
   535	  fi

   574	main() {
   575	  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
   576	    case "$1" in
   577	      --ref)          REF="${2:?--ref needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
   578	      --sha)          SHA="${2:?--sha needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
   579	      --force)        FORCE=1; shift ;;
   580	      --targets)      EXTRA_TARGETS="${2:?--targets needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
   581	      --lock-timeout) LOCK_TIMEOUT="${2:?--lock-timeout needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
   582	      --lease-ttl)    LEASE_TTL="${2:?--lease-ttl needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
   583	      --keep)         KEEP="${2:?--keep needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
   584	      --gc-only)      MODE="gc"; shift ;;
   585	      --status)       MODE="status"; shift ;;
   586	      -h|--help)      usage; exit 0 ;;
   587	      *)              usage >&2; die "unknown argument: $1" ;;
   588	    esac
   589	  done
   590	
   591	  case "$LOCK_TIMEOUT$LEASE_TTL$KEEP" in
   592	    ''|*[!0-9]*) die "--lock-timeout, --lease-ttl and --keep must be non-negative integers" ;;
   593	  esac
   594	
   595	  mkdir -p "$CACHE_ROOT" "$HOT_MAIN" "$SNAPSHOTS" "$LOG_DIR"
   596	
   597	  if [ "$MODE" = "status" ]; then
   598	    print_status
   599	    return 0
   600	  fi
   601	
   602	  # The writer lease is what makes this the *single* writer (DESIGN.md #1).  It is
   603	  # a separate lock from the full-build lock, so a consumer's incremental build can
   604	  # proceed while the warmer sits idle between commits.
   605	  acquire_lock "$LEASE_DIR" "$LEASE_TTL" 0 "warmer-writer-lease" \
   606	    || die "could not acquire the writer lease at $LEASE_DIR"
   607	  LEASE_IDENTITY="$ACQUIRED_LOCK_IDENTITY"
   608	  LEASE_PID="$ACQUIRED_LOCK_PID"
   609	  LEASE_TOKEN="$ACQUIRED_LOCK_TOKEN"
   610	  LEASE_DIGEST="$ACQUIRED_LOCK_DIGEST"
   611	  LEASE_HELD=1
   612	
   613	  if [ "$MODE" = "gc" ]; then
   614	    gc_snapshots
   615	    return 0
   616	  fi
   617	
   618	  local primary sha keyhash target existing_sha existing_status
   619	  local logfile started elapsed status outcome rc name
   620	
   621	  primary="$(resolve_primary_repo)"
   622	  [ -d "$primary/.git" ] || die "$primary is not a git repository; cannot seed the hot main checkout"
   623	
   624	  ensure_lean_on_path
   625	  sha="$(ensure_hot_repo "$primary" "$REF")"
   626	  keyhash="$(compute_keyhash "$HOT_REPO")"
   627	  log "target sha=$sha keyhash=$keyhash"
   628	
   629	  if [ "$FORCE" -eq 0 ] && target="$(current_target)"; then
   630	    existing_sha="$(stamp_field "$target/STAMP" sha || true)"
   631	    existing_status="$(stamp_field "$target/STAMP" status || true)"
   632	    if [ "$existing_sha" = "$sha" ] \
   633	       && [ "$existing_status" = "complete" ] \
   634	       && [ "$(stamp_field "$target/STAMP" keyhash || true)" = "$keyhash" ]; then
   635	      log "a complete snapshot for $sha is already published; nothing to do (use --force to rebuild)"
   636	      gc_snapshots
   637	      return 0
   638	    fi
   639	  fi
   640	
   641	  # One full `lake build` machine-wide (DESIGN.md #7).  The warmer WAITS instead of
   642	  # aborting, and is never killed for a newer commit: pr-ci.yml:50 — "Do not cancel
   643	  # main-branch runs: they seed the build cache."
   644	  if ! acquire_lock \
   645	      "$FULL_BUILD_LOCK" "$LOCK_TIMEOUT" "$LOCK_TIMEOUT" "full-lake-build"; then
   646	    die "could not acquire the machine-wide full-build lock $FULL_BUILD_LOCK \
   647	within ${LOCK_TIMEOUT}s"
   648	  fi
   649	  FULL_BUILD_LOCK_IDENTITY="$ACQUIRED_LOCK_IDENTITY"
   650	  FULL_BUILD_LOCK_PID="$ACQUIRED_LOCK_PID"
   651	  FULL_BUILD_LOCK_TOKEN="$ACQUIRED_LOCK_TOKEN"
   652	  FULL_BUILD_LOCK_DIGEST="$ACQUIRED_LOCK_DIGEST"
   653	  FULL_BUILD_LOCK_HELD=1
   654	
   655	  logfile="$LOG_DIR/warm-$(stamp_id)-${sha:0:12}.log"
   656	  started="$(epoch_now)"
   657	  status="partial"
   658	  outcome="failed"
   659	  rc=0
   660	
   661	  log "building $sha in $HOT_REPO (log: $logfile)"
   662	  seed_hot_repo_lake "$primary"
   663	  proofwidgets_fresh_state_workaround "$HOT_REPO"
   664	  printf '=== cache-warmer %s sha=%s keyhash=%s ===\n' "$(iso_now)" "$sha" "$keyhash" > "$logfile"
   665	
   666	  # No `lake update` here.  `lake exe cache get` fetches Mathlib oleans into
   667	  # .lake/packages; `lake update` would move lake-manifest.json out from under the
   668	  # keyhash and mutate the vendored package trees (two-tier split, see
   669	  # local/protocols/build-cache.md).
   670	  if ! ( cd "$HOT_REPO" && run_outside_git_env lake exe cache get ) >> "$logfile" 2>&1; then
   671	    warn "lake exe cache get failed; continuing to build from source (see $logfile)"
   672	  fi
   673	
   674	  if ( cd "$HOT_REPO" && run_outside_git_env lake build ) >> "$logfile" 2>&1; then
   675	    status="complete"
   676	    outcome="success"
   677	  else
   678	    rc=1
   679	    # pr-ci.yml:161-162 — "Save even when the build failed: a partial cache still
   680	    # spares the next run the modules that did compile."
   681	    warn "lake build failed; publishing a PARTIAL snapshot (see $logfile)"
   682	  fi
   683	
   684	  if [ "$status" = "complete" ] && [ -n "$EXTRA_TARGETS" ]; then
   685	    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
   686	    if ! ( cd "$HOT_REPO" && run_outside_git_env lake build $EXTRA_TARGETS ) >> "$logfile" 2>&1; then
   687	      status="partial"
   688	      outcome="failed"
   689	      rc=1
   690	      warn "extra targets ($EXTRA_TARGETS) failed; the snapshot is flagged partial"
   691	    fi
   692	  fi
   693	
   694	  elapsed=$(( $(epoch_now) - started ))
   695	
   696	  release_lock "$FULL_BUILD_LOCK" "$FULL_BUILD_LOCK_IDENTITY" \
   697	    "$FULL_BUILD_LOCK_PID" "$FULL_BUILD_LOCK_TOKEN" "$FULL_BUILD_LOCK_DIGEST"
   698	  FULL_BUILD_LOCK_HELD=0
   699	
   700	  if [ ! -d "$HOT_REPO/.lake/build" ]; then
   701	    append_build_telemetry "warm" "failed" "$elapsed" "cache-warmer ref=$REF" "$sha" \
   702	      "no .lake/build produced; nothing published; log=$logfile"
   703	    die "no .lake/build directory was produced; nothing to publish (see $logfile)"
   704	  fi
   705	
   706	  name="$(publish_snapshot "$sha" "$keyhash" "$status" "$elapsed")"
   707	  log "published $name (status=$status, ${elapsed}s); current -> $SNAPSHOTS/$name"
   708	
   709	  gc_snapshots
   710	  append_build_telemetry "warm" "$outcome" "$elapsed" "cache-warmer ref=$REF" "$sha" \
   711	    "snapshot=$name status=$status keyhash=$keyhash log=$logfile"
   712	
   713	  return "$rc"
   714	}

   149	# acquire_lock <lockdir> <wait-seconds> <label>
   150	# Per-PR review lock and branch fix reservation. runtime_lock.py serializes
   151	# acquisition, stale recovery, cancellation checks, and owned release.
   152	acquire_lock() {
   153	  local dir="$1" wait_s="$2" label="$3" waited=0 token result rc=0
   154	  local state identity holder observed_token digest detail
   155	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dir")"
   156	  token="$(python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/runtime_lock.py" new-token)" || \
   157	    die "cannot allocate a unique runtime-lock token"
   158	  while :; do
   159	    rc=0
   160	    result="$(python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/runtime_lock.py" acquire \
   161	      "$dir" "$$" "$token" "$label")" || rc=$?
   162	    IFS='|' read -r state identity holder observed_token digest detail <<EOF
   163	$result
   164	EOF
   165	    LOCK_LAST_STATE="$state"
   166	    LOCK_LAST_PID="$holder"
   167	    LOCK_LAST_DETAIL="$detail"
   168	    if [ "$state" = acquired ]; then
   169	      ACQUIRED_LOCK_IDENTITY="$identity"
   170	      ACQUIRED_LOCK_PID="$holder"
   171	      ACQUIRED_LOCK_TOKEN="$observed_token"
   172	      ACQUIRED_LOCK_DIGEST="$digest"
   173	      HELD_LOCKS="${HELD_LOCKS}${HELD_LOCKS:+
   174	}${dir}	${identity}	${holder}	${observed_token}	${digest}"
   175	      [ -z "$detail" ] || warn "$detail at $dir"
   176	      return 0
   177	    fi
   178	    if [ "$state" = unsafe ] || [ "$rc" -eq 2 ]; then
   179	      die "unsafe runtime lock $dir: ${detail:-helper failure}; recover that exact path manually"
   180	    fi
   181	    if [ "$waited" -ge "$wait_s" ]; then
   182	      die "timed out after ${wait_s}s waiting for the review lock $dir \
   183	(holder pid ${holder:-unknown})"
   184	    fi
   185	    [ "$waited" = 0 ] && log "another review holds $dir (pid ${holder:-unknown}); queuing"
   186	    sleep 5
   187	    waited=$((waited + 5))
   188	  done
   189	}

    48	CI checks cleanliness after binding the initial comparison and again at every

   191	Merge reserves the CI, review, and fix runtime directories through the same
   192	helper as their ordinary owners. Each claim contains the directory device/inode
   193	identity, PID, random UUID token, and digest of structured owner metadata. The
   194	persistent sibling `flock` serializes creation, validation, cancellation, stale
   195	recovery, and release. Under it, any transition based on a prior observation
   196	must match the complete claim before the canonical path is renamed or a

   199	A directory without a complete valid owner may be a stale partial lock or an

   201	age. The operator must verify that no CI, review, auto-fix, merge, or build

With two stale breakers, breaker A can remove the stale lock and acquire its replacement; breaker B can then rename that replacement, discover the inode mismatch, and temporarily leave the canonical path absent. A third contender can acquire the canonical name, causing the real replacement to remain stranded under `.stale.*` at [line 173](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0007-github-native-workflow/local/bin/ci.sh:173). Serialization is therefore not preserved.

   Minimal fix: serialize every stale-break and release transition using one stable per-lock mutex shared by shell and Python, such as `flock` on a sibling file. Revalidate inode or token while holding that mutex before renaming.

   Required regression: deterministically pause breaker B after it observes the stale inode, let breaker A remove it and acquire the replacement, then resume B while a third contender attempts acquisition. Assert the replacement is never renamed and only one owner enters. The existing sequential partial-lock test at [test_github_workflow.py:1708](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0007-github-native-workflow/scripts/tests/test_github_workflow.py:1708) does not exercise this race.

  review accepted failed CI and permissively normalized malformed reviewer

  review; and auto-fix did not bind the fetched base through dispatch, commit,
  and push. Reviewer identities and trusted refs also admitted replay or
  unlike-string equality gaps. Diagnosis: full-SHA markers protected remote
  objects, but the producer-side tree, lock lease, parser grammar, evidence
  completion state, and base comparison were not one contract. Fix: require a
  clean committed tree at producer boundaries, ownership-stamped shared fix
  leases, success-only CI review gating, strict state-preserving findings
  parsing, attestation-only consumers plus exact summary recovery, resolved
  trusted commits, cross-attestation identity uniqueness, and full head/base
  checks throughout auto-fix. The final implementation audit also found that a
  cancel arriving after a wrapper commit could strand the unpublished local
  tip; the fix stops further dispatches but permits its ownership-checked,
  original-head leased publication handoff. A second final audit found boundary
  tail, idempotency-lookup, replay preflight, run-id, and summary
  reclassification races; in-process mutation guards, pre-POST identity
  validation, unique attestation run ids, structured findings consumption, and
  one guarded finalizer close them. The closing shell audit additionally found
  that review-fix read its count and body in separate snapshots, a late cancel
  could strand a wrapper commit, phase failures could be masked by Bash's
  conditional `errexit` semantics, and signal traps could report success. It
  also exposed findings/trailer prefix lookalikes and arbitrary backticked text
  passing as canonical locations. Fix: consume one parsed attestation snapshot,
  make cancellation ownership-only for every boundary after local advancement,
  test fallible phase commands explicitly, preserve signal exit status during
  owned-lock cleanup, and require prefix-safe section/trailer sentinels plus
  relative path-and-line locations.
  Lesson: exact-head evidence is trustworthy only when the local committed
  state and every transition to publication are bound as rigorously as the
  remote marker.

  summary, adverse local reviews could attempt sticky `REQUEST_CHANGES`, merge

  free-form adjudication path did not prove its review rounds or dispositions.

  lease alongside the review/fix leases. Diagnosis: exact-head client checks

  checks, base freshness, and merge policy. Fix: publish pending then

**Findings**

1. **High: a lease can be reclaimed while protected child processes remain alive.** [runtime_lock.py:272](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0007-github-native-workflow/local/bin/runtime_lock.py:272) determines staleness solely from the recorded PID, and [runtime_lock.py:325](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0007-github-native-workflow/local/bin/runtime_lock.py:325) removes that lease once the PID disappears. Shell callers record `$$`, including `ci.sh:161`, `review.sh:160`, `autofix.sh:158`, `cache-warmer.sh:172`, `warm-worktree.sh:155`, and `housekeeping.sh:212`, while protected work runs in descendants such as [ci.sh:1100](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0007-github-native-workflow/local/bin/ci.sh:1100) and [autofix.sh:955](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0007-github-native-workflow/local/bin/autofix.sh:955). If the wrapper alone is killed, the surviving build/fixer can overlap a new owner after stale recovery. The lease needs process-tree lifetime or an inherited kernel-held lease, not just wrapper-PID lifetime.

2. **High: the default write-enabled human agent remains outside the fix-lock protocol.** [agent.sh:153](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0007-github-native-workflow/local/bin/agent.sh:153) defaults to `workspace-write`, but [agent.sh:286](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0007-github-native-workflow/local/bin/agent.sh:286) only performs an unlocked PID snapshot before dispatch at [agent.sh:381](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0007-github-native-workflow/local/bin/agent.sh:381). It proceeds on partial/malformed records and holds no reservation afterward, so autofix or review can acquire the branch lock while that agent writes.

3. **Medium: signal traps can release locks yet continue or report success.** [housekeeping.sh:224](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0007-github-native-workflow/local/bin/housekeeping.sh:224) handles `INT`/`TERM` with a function that returns, allowing execution to continue at line 225 after releasing the full-build lock. [cache-warmer.sh:206](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0007-github-native-workflow/local/bin/cache-warmer.sh:206) and [warm-worktree.sh:195](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0007-github-native-workflow/local/bin/warm-worktree.sh:195) capture the previous `$?`; a signal arriving after a successful command therefore exits zero. Isolated Bash reproductions confirmed both continuation and exit status `0`.

4. **Medium: cancellation is not serialized with the final GitHub write.** The last lease validation ends at [github_api.py:1235](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0007-github-native-workflow/local/bin/github_api.py:1235). Review and status mutations then release the transition mutex before their POSTs at [github_api.py:2131](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0007-github-native-workflow/local/bin/github_api.py:2131) and [github_api.py:1937](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0007-github-native-workflow/local/bin/github_api.py:1937). A cancellation can be committed between those operations, yet clean evidence is still published and no post-write lease validation occurs.

5. **Low: oversized PID records escape fail-closed handling.** [runtime_lock.py:180](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0007-github-native-workflow/local/bin/runtime_lock.py:180) accepts an arbitrary-length decimal PID. `os.kill` at line 276 then raises uncaught `OverflowError`; the top-level handler at line 623 does not catch it. This was reproduced with a 64-bit-exceeding PID and produces a traceback instead of an `unsafe` result.

**Test Gaps**

The 101-test workflow suite could not execute because the read-only sandbox had no writable temporary directory; every case stopped in `TemporaryDirectory` setup. Bash syntax, Python AST parsing, and `git diff --check HEAD` passed.

Coverage is still missing for a dead wrapper with a surviving child, foreign-host records, the three utility signal paths, `agent.sh` against partial/new locks, and cancellation after the final guard but before POST. The fake merge test injects an adverse review during an earlier read, not at the server mutation boundary.

COMMENT-only, zero-approval semantics remain intact at [github_api.py:2049](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0007-github-native-workflow/local/bin/github_api.py:2049) and [pr_merge.py:231](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0007-github-native-workflow/local/bin/pr_merge.py:231). I found no direct rename/delete of shared workflow lock paths outside `runtime_lock.py`, and no additional replacement-directory or lock-order deadlock defect.

No files or Git/GitHub state were changed; no Lean or blueprint commands ran.
